key_insight: Ferroelectric polarization switching in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 occurs through a cooperative O3c/O4c oxygen-exchange pathway with a transient bond-formation detour, rather than a simple displacement-only mechanism.
engineering_relevance: This dynamic atomistic mechanism explains how HZO can switch polarization stably without macroscopic strain, supporting design rules for durable and scalable non-volatile ferroelectric memories.
method: Electric-field-induced molecular dynamics simulations were run on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice.
A fine-tuned MACEField machine-learning force field was used to capture switching dynamics.
Atomic trajectories were analyzed to identify coordination changes, transient cation–oxygen bonding, and local volume compensation.
evidence_signal: The simulation dynamically reproduced the P–E hysteresis loop and revealed coordinated oxygen exchange, detour behavior, and internal self-compensation during switching.
watch_item: The results are based on an ideal defect-free lattice, so real-device defects, interfaces, and processing variability may alter the switching pathway.
paper_title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
